name: virtual-list
purpose: Renders only the visible items (plus an overscan) of very large lists, 100,000 items and more, with fixed or measured variable heights. Selectable lists are WAI-ARIA listboxes with single or multiple selection, type-ahead, and roving focus; otherwise the list is a plain role=list. The focused item always stays rendered. aui-range-change reports the visible range for lazy loading, and an optional loadMore hook adds infinite scroll with a polite status message.
whenToUse: Lists of hundreds to millions of items, such as people, files, or log lines.
A selectable list in a sidebar or picker that must stay fast with large data.
Infinite scroll over a paged API.
whenNotToUse: Short lists (under a few hundred items): render them directly or use Sortable List.
Tabular data with columns, sorting, and filters: use Data Table or Data Grid (both virtualize).
Lists the user must print or search with the browser's find: only visible items are in the DOM.
responsive: Fills the inline size of its host; the block size comes from the height option or, with height null, from the host (for example a Splitter pane). The rendered window follows the viewport size.
rtl: Items, the selection bar, and text follow the writing direction; the scrollbar sits on the inline-end edge as the browser places it.
theme: Component tokens virtual-list-radius (radius-md) and virtual-list-border-color (color-border). Selected items use color-selected and color-selected-text plus a start-edge bar (color-selected-indicator), so selection is not shown by color alone; forced colors use Highlight and HighlightText.
security: Items are rendered by the application's renderItem as DOM nodes; the component never parses HTML. Status messages are set as text.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. loadMore is the application's own function.

performance.testedScale: 100,000 fixed-height and variable-height items; at most 1,000,000 items, and items x height must stay under the browser's maximum element height (about 17.9 million px in Firefox, 33.5 million px in Chromium): 400,000 items of 40 px work everywhere.

limitations: The total height (items x item height) must stay under the browser's maximum element height, about 17.9 million px in Firefox.
Only rendered items exist in the DOM, so the browser's find-in-page and printing see only those.
Variable heights are estimated until an item has been rendered once, so the scrollbar can adjust while scrolling.
unsupported: Drag-and-drop reordering (use Sortable List for short lists).
antiPatterns: Returning the same Node from renderItem for different calls; items are rendered again as they scroll back into view.
Using index keys (the default) with selection while items are inserted or removed: pass itemKey.
